analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift head text lines 1-1046 (two units) plus the patch excerpt. The excerpt shows the actual changes are in the memory-reclamation helpers around lines 1309-1349 and 1396-1412 of the head file. Those lines are not in the supplied head units, so they were reviewed only through the truncated patch.

The visible changes: `reclaimableMemoryBytes` now also counts `CBv2RetainedKVSegments.retainedBytes`. A new `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad` calls `GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments()` and then clears the MLX cache. `evictUntilAvailable` gains a `poolDropped` flag based on `busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory()`. These are memory-accounting and availability logic. They touch no trust boundary, key, attestation, authorization or coordinator protocol. The security-relevant surface is T-028 (residual KV and GPU data) and T-029/T-010 (availability). Releasing retained free KV segments earlier does not obviously weaken T-028 and may help it.

Unchanged code visible in the units has a fail-closed weight-hash flow (T-041 and the T-012/T-027 family). Fresh cryptographic hashes bracket the load for reusable SSD cache or profile requirements. The SSD cache eligibility hash is published only when the pre-load and post-load hashes match. A mismatch aborts before slot install, and a missing hash disables SSD reuse (`markWeightHashUnavailable`). This code is unchanged in the patch excerpt.

Residual questions for integration:
1. The truncated patch (the `evictUntilAvailable` body) and the definitions of `CBv2RetainedKVSegments`, `GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments` and `busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory` were not visible.
2. Whether the brief wait in `releaseRetainedKVSegments` can stall the load gate or actor is unverified. That is an availability question only, with no concrete evidence of a regression.
3. Whether the accounting can over-count reclaimable memory and lead to over-admission is unverified.
